questions.prompt: In Grade 10 CRE, why is the Bible described as inspired Scripture?
options: It is understood by Christians as God's message communicated through human writers
It was written by one author in one year
It only contains songs and poems
It is used only as a history textbook
questions.correctAnswer: It is understood by Christians as God's message communicated through human writers
questions.explanation: Christian teaching treats the Bible as sacred writing through which God guides faith and moral living.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why Christians value the Bible as inspired Scripture.

questions.prompt: Which grouping best represents common categories of books in the Old Testament?
options: Law, Historical Books, Wisdom Writings, and Prophets
Gospels, Acts, Letters, and Revelation
Poems, Newspapers, Diaries, and Novels
Maps, Charts, Speeches, and Timetables
questions.correctAnswer: Law, Historical Books, Wisdom Writings, and Prophets
questions.explanation: The Old Testament is commonly organized into major sections such as Law, history, wisdom writings, and prophetic books.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify Old Testament books according to their major categories.

questions.prompt: Which literary form is most associated with many Psalms in the Bible?
options: Poetry and song
Laboratory report
Business invoice
Court summons
questions.correctAnswer: Poetry and song
questions.explanation: Many Psalms use poetic language for prayer, praise, lament, and thanksgiving.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify literary forms used in biblical writings.

questions.prompt: A learner compares a Bible passage with its historical background before explaining it. Which Bible study method is being used?
options: Contextual study
Guessing from the title only
Ignoring the passage setting
Memorising without understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Contextual study
questions.explanation: Contextual study considers the setting, audience, and purpose of a passage before applying its message.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate methods to study and interpret biblical texts.

questions.prompt: In the CRE topic on the fall of humankind, what does redemption mainly refer to?
options: God's act of restoring broken relationship with human beings
Human beings becoming unable to make choices
The end of all moral responsibility
A rule that creation no longer matters
questions.correctAnswer: God's act of restoring broken relationship with human beings
questions.explanation: Redemption in Christian teaching points to restoration from sin and renewed relationship with God.
questions.subStrandTitle: Redemption after the Fall of Man
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of redemption after the fall of humankind.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows stewardship over creation in a Kenyan school setting?
options: Organising learners to conserve water and plant trees responsibly
Dumping plastic waste behind classrooms
Wasting food because it is available
Burning vegetation to clear a playing field quickly
questions.correctAnswer: Organising learners to conserve water and plant trees responsibly
questions.explanation: Stewardship means caring responsibly for God's creation, including land, water, plants, animals, and people.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the biblical idea of stewardship to environmental care.

questions.prompt: In the Exodus story, what is the central theme of Israel leaving Egypt?
options: Liberation from oppression and God's guidance
The start of Roman rule
The building of the Jerusalem temple by Solomon
The writing of the New Testament letters
questions.correctAnswer: Liberation from oppression and God's guidance
questions.explanation: The Exodus is remembered in CRE as a story of deliverance, covenant, worship, and dependence on God.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key themes in the Exodus experience.

questions.prompt: Why is the Passover important in the study of the Exodus?
options: It remembers God's deliverance of the Israelites from slavery
It marks the birth of Moses in Canaan
It celebrates the writing of Paul's letters
It replaced all covenant laws at Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: It remembers God's deliverance of the Israelites from slavery
questions.explanation: Passover recalls the events connected with Israel's liberation and is linked to gratitude and remembrance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the religious significance of Passover in the Exodus narrative.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the Sinai Covenant in CRE?
options: An agreement between God and the Israelites with commandments guiding their life
A trade treaty between Egypt and Canaan
A letter written by Paul to Corinth
A parable told during the Galilean ministry
questions.correctAnswer: An agreement between God and the Israelites with commandments guiding their life
questions.explanation: The Sinai Covenant joined worship, obedience, and community life through God's commands.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and purpose of the Sinai Covenant.

questions.prompt: A class discusses how the commandment against stealing applies to misuse of public resources. Which skill are they demonstrating?
options: Applying biblical teaching to contemporary moral issues
Replacing moral teaching with opinion polls
Ignoring the social meaning of commandments
Studying only ancient geography
questions.correctAnswer: Applying biblical teaching to contemporary moral issues
questions.explanation: CBC religious education expects learners to connect scriptural teachings with responsible choices in daily life.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the Ten Commandments to contemporary ethical situations.

questions.prompt: In the story of Elijah on Mount Carmel, what quality is most clearly tested?
options: Loyalty to God
Skill in farming
Knowledge of Roman law
Ability to speak Greek
questions.correctAnswer: Loyalty to God
questions.explanation: The Elijah narratives challenge people to reject idolatry and remain faithful to God.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify lessons on loyalty to God from the ministry of Elijah.

questions.prompt: Which situation best reflects loyalty to God in a learner's daily life from a CRE perspective?
options: Refusing to join cheating even when friends apply pressure
Mocking classmates who disagree
Hiding a mistake to protect reputation
Using prayer as an excuse to avoid duties
questions.correctAnswer: Refusing to join cheating even when friends apply pressure
questions.explanation: Loyalty includes faithfulness, courage, and moral consistency when choices are difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate lessons from Elijah to responsible decision-making.

questions.prompt: What was a major role of Old Testament prophets?
options: Calling people back to justice, faithfulness, and obedience to God
Serving only as palace entertainers
Writing scientific manuals for farmers
Replacing all community leaders permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Calling people back to justice, faithfulness, and obedience to God
questions.explanation: Prophets challenged wrongdoing, warned against injustice, and reminded people of covenant obligations.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of prophets in Old Testament society.

questions.prompt: Which concern is strongly associated with the teachings of Prophet Amos?
options: Social justice and sincere worship
Shipbuilding and ocean navigation
The birth stories of Jesus
The spread of the Umayyad dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: Social justice and sincere worship
questions.explanation: Amos criticised exploitation and empty worship, insisting that justice and righteousness matter.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarize key teachings of Prophet Amos.

questions.prompt: A church youth group plans a campaign against corruption and unfair treatment of workers. Which teaching of Amos best supports the campaign?
options: Justice should be visible in community life, not only in religious words
Wealth always proves moral goodness
Worship should ignore treatment of the poor
Leaders should never be questioned
questions.correctAnswer: Justice should be visible in community life, not only in religious words
questions.explanation: Amos connects true worship with justice, honesty, and care for vulnerable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply prophetic teachings on justice to contemporary society.

questions.prompt: Which set names major categories of New Testament books?
options: Gospels, Acts, Letters, and Revelation
Law, Prophets, Psalms, and Proverbs
Hadith, Fiqh, Akhlaq, and Sirah
Vedas, Upanishads, Epics, and Puranas
questions.correctAnswer: Gospels, Acts, Letters, and Revelation
questions.explanation: The New Testament includes the Gospels, Acts, epistles or letters, and Revelation.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify New Testament books according to their major categories.

questions.prompt: What is the main value of studying the infancy and early life of Jesus in CRE?
options: It helps learners understand Christian beliefs about Jesus' identity and mission
It explains the full history of the Roman Empire
It replaces the study of Jesus' ministry
It gives rules for modern banking
questions.correctAnswer: It helps learners understand Christian beliefs about Jesus' identity and mission
questions.explanation: The infancy narratives introduce themes of promise, obedience, humility, and God's purpose.
questions.subStrandTitle: Infancy and Early Life of Jesus Christ
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the significance of the infancy and early life narratives of Jesus.

questions.prompt: Which activity was central to the Galilean ministry of Jesus?
options: Teaching, healing, calling disciples, and proclaiming God's kingdom
Building the Jerusalem temple
Writing all New Testament letters
Leading the Exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching, healing, calling disciples, and proclaiming God's kingdom
questions.explanation: The Galilean ministry presents Jesus as teacher, healer, and caller of disciples.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe major activities in the Galilean ministry of Jesus.

questions.prompt: Why did Jesus often use parables in his teaching?
options: To communicate spiritual and moral lessons through familiar stories
To hide all meaning from ordinary listeners
To replace worship with entertainment
To record government laws word for word
questions.correctAnswer: To communicate spiritual and moral lessons through familiar stories
questions.explanation: Parables use everyday situations to invite reflection on faith, values, and conduct.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the purpose of parables in the teaching ministry of Jesus.

questions.prompt: In Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians, which issue is addressed when believers are urged to value unity?
options: Division within the Christian community
Construction of the pyramids
Compilation of the Qur'an
Classification of Hindu dances
questions.correctAnswer: Division within the Christian community
questions.explanation: Paul wrote to correct divisions and encourage love, order, and responsible use of gifts.
questions.subStrandTitle: Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians
questions.learningOutcome: Identify community issues addressed in Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians.

questions.prompt: A learner says spiritual gifts should make a person superior to others. Which response best fits Paul's teaching in 1 Corinthians?
options: Gifts are for serving and building the community in love
Gifts prove that some people should never listen
Gifts are useful only when they create competition
Gifts remove the need for moral conduct
questions.correctAnswer: Gifts are for serving and building the community in love
questions.explanation: Paul presents gifts as resources for service, unity, and love, not for pride.
questions.subStrandTitle: Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Paul's teaching on gifts and love to community life.

questions.prompt: In CRE, Pentecost is mainly linked with which Christian belief?
options: The coming of the Holy Spirit upon the early believers
The giving of the Ten Commandments at Sinai
The rise of the Umayyad dynasty
The first Buddhist council
questions.correctAnswer: The coming of the Holy Spirit upon the early believers
questions.explanation: Pentecost is studied as a key event in which the Holy Spirit empowered the early church.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the role of the Holy Spirit in the early church.

questions.prompt: Which use of a gift of the Holy Spirit best shows responsible Christian service?
options: Using leadership ability to organize fair support for needy learners
Using influence to embarrass weaker classmates
Refusing accountability because one is gifted
Demanding payment before helping anyone
questions.correctAnswer: Using leadership ability to organize fair support for needy learners
questions.explanation: Gifts are expected to promote service, compassion, order, and the common good.
questions.subStrandTitle: The Gifts of the Holy Spirit
questions.learningOutcome: Apply teachings on gifts of the Holy Spirit to service in society.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the Christian doctrine of the Holy Trinity?
options: One God understood as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
Three unrelated gods competing for power
A teaching about the four Gospels only
A rule about the order of church buildings
questions.correctAnswer: One God understood as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The Trinity is a central Christian belief about one God revealed as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the basic meaning of the doctrine of the Holy Trinity.

questions.prompt: Which pair is commonly taught as sacraments in many Christian traditions?
options: Baptism and Eucharist
Zakat and Hajj
Karma and Dharma
Diwali and Holi
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism and Eucharist
questions.explanation: Baptism and Eucharist are widely recognized Christian sacraments, though practices vary across churches.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common sacraments and their place in Christian worship.

questions.prompt: When making a moral decision, which approach best fits Christian ethics in Grade 10 CRE?
options: Consider Scripture, conscience, community wellbeing, and responsible consequences
Choose whatever brings quickest personal gain
Ignore people affected by the decision
Follow rumours without checking facts
questions.correctAnswer: Consider Scripture, conscience, community wellbeing, and responsible consequences
questions.explanation: Christian ethics encourages informed choices guided by faith, conscience, love of neighbour, and responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Use Christian ethical principles to guide moral decision-making.

questions.prompt: A CRE discussion links human rights with action against gender-based violence. Which statement best reflects the lesson?
options: Every person has dignity and should be protected from abuse
Violence is acceptable if it is hidden
Rights apply only to adults with authority
Faith communities should ignore abuse
questions.correctAnswer: Every person has dignity and should be protected from abuse
questions.explanation: Human dignity and protection from violence are central to respectful, ethical community life.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Christian teaching on dignity to human rights and protection from violence.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows responsible handling of human sexuality from a CRE perspective?
options: Respecting personal dignity, boundaries, self-control, and accurate guidance
Sharing private information to entertain friends
Pressuring another person into a relationship
Treating sexuality as separate from values
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting personal dignity, boundaries, self-control, and accurate guidance
questions.explanation: CRE treats sexuality as an area requiring respect, responsibility, informed choices, and care for others.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Christian values to responsible choices about human sexuality.

questions.prompt: Which value is most important for strengthening marriage and family life in CRE?
options: Mutual respect and faithful responsibility
Secrecy and unfair control
Neglect of children
Avoiding communication in conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Mutual respect and faithful responsibility
questions.explanation: Healthy family life is supported by respect, care, faithfulness, communication, and shared responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain values that support responsible marriage and family life.

questions.prompt: Which statement best reflects a balanced Christian response to modern medicine, science, and technology?
options: Use them responsibly to protect life and dignity while asking ethical questions
Reject every medical service without discussion
Use technology without considering harm
Let science remove all moral responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Use them responsibly to protect life and dignity while asking ethical questions
questions.explanation: CRE encourages learners to appreciate helpful advances while evaluating their moral impact.
questions.subStrandTitle: Christian Response to Modern Medicine, Science and Technology
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate Christian responses to modern medicine, science, and technology.

questions.prompt: A Bible passage is poetic, but a learner interprets it as a literal laboratory description. What is the strongest weakness in that interpretation?
options: It ignores the literary form of the passage
It uses too many Bible references
It compares ideas from the same book
It reads the passage aloud
questions.correctAnswer: It ignores the literary form of the passage
questions.explanation: Accurate Bible study considers genre, setting, language, and purpose before drawing conclusions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how literary form affects interpretation of biblical passages.

questions.prompt: Which example best connects the Sinai Covenant with responsible citizenship today?
options: Promoting honesty, respect for life, and respect for others' property
Using religious language to avoid civic duties
Obeying rules only when being watched
Treating community resources as private property
questions.correctAnswer: Promoting honesty, respect for life, and respect for others' property
questions.explanation: The covenant commandments support values that can guide ethical citizenship and community wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze links between covenant values and responsible citizenship.

questions.prompt: A community holds impressive worship services but underpays workers and exploits poor families. Which Grade 10 CRE theme most directly critiques this contradiction?
options: Prophet Amos on justice and sincere worship
The infancy of Jesus
Classification of New Testament books
The literary form of Psalms only
questions.correctAnswer: Prophet Amos on justice and sincere worship
questions.explanation: Amos challenges religious practice that is separated from justice, fairness, and care for vulnerable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate social practices using prophetic teachings on justice.

questions.prompt: Which project would best synthesize CRE learning on stewardship, human dignity, and service?
options: A school plan combining tree planting, anti-bullying support, and help for vulnerable learners
A contest that rewards only the loudest religious slogans
A campaign to shame learners from other faiths
A report that lists problems but avoids any action
questions.correctAnswer: A school plan combining tree planting, anti-bullying support, and help for vulnerable learners
questions.explanation: A strong project combines knowledge, values, and practical action for people and the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Select practical actions that integrate CRE values in community service.

questions.prompt: In Grade 10 IRE, what does the compilation of the Qur'an refer to?
options: Gathering the revealed text into an organized written collection
Translating every verse into one modern language
Replacing recitation with poetry
Writing a biography of every caliph
questions.correctAnswer: Gathering the revealed text into an organized written collection
questions.explanation: Compilation concerns the careful gathering and preservation of the Qur'anic text.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.subStrandTitle: Compilation and Standardization of the Qur'an
questions.learningOutcome: Define compilation and standardization in relation to the Qur'an.

questions.prompt: Why was standardization of the Qur'an important as Islam spread to new regions?
options: It helped preserve uniform reading and reduce disputes in recitation
It removed the need to learn Arabic letters
It made Hadith unnecessary
It allowed each town to create a different Qur'an
questions.correctAnswer: It helped preserve uniform reading and reduce disputes in recitation
questions.explanation: Standardization supported consistency and preservation as Muslim communities expanded.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.subStrandTitle: Compilation and Standardization of the Qur'an
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for standardizing the Qur'anic text.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of diacritical marks in Qur'anic Arabic?
options: To guide pronunciation and reduce reading errors
To decorate pages without meaning
To divide the Qur'an into historical periods
To replace memorization completely
questions.correctAnswer: To guide pronunciation and reduce reading errors
questions.explanation: Diacritical marks help readers pronounce words accurately, especially non-native Arabic readers.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of diacritical marks in Qur'anic reading.

questions.prompt: In Qur'anic studies, what is a Makkan verse commonly associated with?
options: Revelation before the Hijrah, often emphasizing faith and moral warning
A verse written only in Medina after the Hijrah
A Hadith with a weak chain
A ruling about modern employment contracts
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation before the Hijrah, often emphasizing faith and moral warning
questions.explanation: Makkan and Madinan classifications help learners understand context, audience, and themes of revelation.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish Qur'anic verses by context and theme.

questions.prompt: What does Asbab al-Nuzul help a learner understand?
options: The circumstances or reasons connected with a revelation
The number of pages in a printed copy
The family tree of every narrator
The rules for Indian classical dance
questions.correctAnswer: The circumstances or reasons connected with a revelation
questions.explanation: Asbab al-Nuzul gives background that supports careful interpretation of Qur'anic passages.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of reasons for revelation in Qur'anic interpretation.

questions.prompt: Selected verses from Surah al-Furqan 25:61-77 are often studied for which broad theme?
options: Qualities of faithful servants and moral conduct
Rules for measuring farm produce only
The history of the Roman senate
The classification of New Testament letters
questions.correctAnswer: Qualities of faithful servants and moral conduct
questions.explanation: The selected passage highlights humility, devotion, self-control, and responsible conduct.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Identify moral qualities taught in selected verses from Surah al-Furqan.

questions.prompt: In Ulum al-Hadith, what is the isnad?
options: The chain of narrators through whom a Hadith was transmitted
The main text of the Hadith itself
A type of special prayer
A tax record for Zakat distribution
questions.correctAnswer: The chain of narrators through whom a Hadith was transmitted
questions.explanation: The isnad helps scholars assess transmission, while the matn is the content of the report.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between isnad and matn in Hadith studies.

questions.prompt: Why is the matn studied carefully in Hadith scholarship?
options: It contains the actual reported teaching or action being examined
It is the list of narrators only
It is always a map of Arabia
It gives the price of books in a market
questions.correctAnswer: It contains the actual reported teaching or action being examined
questions.explanation: The matn is studied for meaning, consistency, and guidance alongside the reliability of transmission.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of matn in evaluating Hadith.

questions.prompt: Which situation best applies a Hadith value on honesty in school life?
options: Returning a lost calculator to the teacher without taking it
Changing marks in a report book
Copying answers during a test
Spreading unverified rumours about a classmate
questions.correctAnswer: Returning a lost calculator to the teacher without taking it
questions.explanation: Hadith teachings on honesty guide Muslims to act truthfully and protect other people's rights.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic moral teachings on honesty to daily situations.

questions.prompt: Which prayer is an example of a special occasion prayer in Islam?
options: Salat al-Janazah
A school assembly roll call
A parliamentary oath
A business receipt
questions.correctAnswer: Salat al-Janazah
questions.explanation: Salat al-Janazah is a funeral prayer and is studied under special occasion prayers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of prayers performed on special occasions.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best names key Muslim funeral rites studied in Grade 10 IRE?
options: Ghusl, kafan, funeral prayer, and burial
Baptism, Eucharist, confirmation, and marriage
Aarti, bhajan, prasad, and garba
Voting, taxation, licensing, and auditing
questions.correctAnswer: Ghusl, kafan, funeral prayer, and burial
questions.explanation: Islamic funeral rites include washing, shrouding, funeral prayer, and burial with dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe major rites performed for the deceased in Islam.

questions.prompt: What is the main social purpose of proper Zakat administration?
options: To support eligible recipients and promote social welfare
To enrich only the collector
To replace all forms of work
To make charity secret from the needy
questions.correctAnswer: To support eligible recipients and promote social welfare
questions.explanation: Zakat administration should be accountable and directed to eligible groups to strengthen welfare and justice.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose and ethical administration of Zakat.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide discussion of divorce in IRE?
options: Justice, responsibility, and protection of family rights
Public humiliation of families
Ignoring children and dependants
Using divorce as a joke or threat
questions.correctAnswer: Justice, responsibility, and protection of family rights
questions.explanation: The topic is handled respectfully, with attention to rights, duties, reconciliation, and dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic values when discussing family responsibilities and divorce.

questions.prompt: A Muslim community sets up counselling, financial support, and inheritance guidance for widows. Which IRE value is mainly shown?
options: Care and justice for vulnerable members of society
Competition for public praise
Neglect of family obligations
Discouragement of community service
questions.correctAnswer: Care and justice for vulnerable members of society
questions.explanation: IRE emphasizes dignity, protection, and fair treatment for widows and other vulnerable persons.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Islamic teachings to care for widows and vulnerable people.

questions.prompt: In Islamic governance, what does shura mean?
options: Consultation in decision-making
Rule by secrecy only
Buying public office
Avoiding accountability
questions.correctAnswer: Consultation in decision-making
questions.explanation: Shura supports participatory, accountable, and fair decision-making.
questions.learningOutcome: Define shura and relate it to accountable governance.

questions.prompt: Which workplace practice best reflects Islamic labour relations?
options: Paying workers fairly and respecting agreed duties
Delaying wages without reason
Forcing unsafe work without protection
Dismissing workers for asking lawful questions
questions.correctAnswer: Paying workers fairly and respecting agreed duties
questions.explanation: Islamic labour ethics value fairness, honesty, safety, and fulfilment of agreements.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic teachings to fair labour relations.

questions.prompt: Which practice best reflects ethical Da'wah in a multi-faith Kenyan society?
options: Sharing Islamic teachings respectfully without coercion or insults
Mocking people of other faiths
Using false information to win arguments
Pressuring learners during examinations
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing Islamic teachings respectfully without coercion or insults
questions.explanation: Ethical Da'wah is guided by wisdom, respect, truthfulness, and peaceful relations.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical principles when explaining religious teachings to others.

questions.prompt: Which food category is prohibited in the Grade 10 IRE topic on foods and drinks?
options: Pork
Clean water
Ripe mangoes
Boiled rice
questions.correctAnswer: Pork
questions.explanation: IRE covers prohibited foods and drinks, including pork, carrion, blood, and intoxicants.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify foods and drinks prohibited in Islamic teaching.

questions.prompt: What is the main moral aim of Islamic guidance on clothing and adornment?
options: Modesty, dignity, and respect in personal presentation
Competition through expensive fashion
Humiliating people with fewer clothes
Rejecting neatness and cleanliness
questions.correctAnswer: Modesty, dignity, and respect in personal presentation
questions.explanation: Islamic teaching links clothing with modesty, cleanliness, dignity, and respect for self and others.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain moral values connected with Islamic clothing and adornment.

questions.prompt: A learner walks through a crowded market calmly, avoids arrogance, and respects other people. Which Akhlaq topic is being applied?
options: Manners of walking
Administration of Zakat
Types of Qur'anic verses
Rise of the Umayyad dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: Manners of walking
questions.explanation: Akhlaq includes everyday manners, including humility and respect in movement and public conduct.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic etiquette to public behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows avoiding prohibitions in Islam in a school context?
options: Declining to take part in bullying and dishonest gain
Joining gossip to become popular
Taking another learner's property secretly
Helping friends hide harmful behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Declining to take part in bullying and dishonest gain
questions.explanation: Avoiding prohibited conduct protects dignity, honesty, safety, and peaceful relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic moral prohibitions to everyday conduct.

questions.prompt: Which dynasty is studied in Grade 10 IRE under Islamic History and Civilisation?
options: The Umayyad dynasty
The Ming dynasty
The Tudor dynasty
The Ptolemaic dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: The Umayyad dynasty
questions.explanation: Grade 10 IRE includes the rise, selected leaders, achievements, and decline of the Umayyad dynasty.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the Muslim dynasty studied in Grade 10 IRE.

questions.prompt: Which leader is commonly associated with the establishment of Umayyad rule?
options: Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan
Prophet Amos
Guru Nanak
Emperor Ashoka
questions.correctAnswer: Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan
questions.explanation: Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan is studied as a key figure in the rise of the Umayyad dynasty.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected leaders connected with the Umayyad dynasty.

questions.prompt: Which achievement is often linked with Abdul Malik ibn Marwan?
options: Administrative reforms and use of Arabic in state administration
Writing the Gospels
Starting Jain monastic orders
Composing the Psalms of David
questions.correctAnswer: Administrative reforms and use of Arabic in state administration
questions.explanation: Abdul Malik is remembered for reforms that strengthened administration and identity in the Umayyad state.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain achievements of selected Umayyad leaders.

questions.prompt: Why is Umar ibn Abdulaziz often highlighted in discussions of leadership?
options: He is associated with justice, piety, and administrative reform
He abolished all forms of consultation
He founded the Sinai Covenant
He created the Trimurti doctrine
questions.correctAnswer: He is associated with justice, piety, and administrative reform
questions.explanation: Umar ibn Abdulaziz is often studied as an example of ethical leadership and reform.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze leadership values shown by selected Umayyad caliphs.

questions.prompt: A learner argues that Zakat must be transparent because it affects public trust. Which IRE principle supports this view?
options: Accountability in managing community resources
Secrecy in all financial records
Preference for the wealthy only
Avoidance of helping eligible recipients
questions.correctAnswer: Accountability in managing community resources
questions.explanation: Zakat administration requires honesty, fairness, and accountable distribution to eligible recipients.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze accountability in the administration of Zakat.

questions.prompt: Which option best compares shura with democratic participation?
options: Both value consultation, voice, and responsibility in decision-making
Both require leaders to ignore the community
Both reject justice as a public concern
Both forbid any accountability after decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Both value consultation, voice, and responsibility in decision-making
questions.explanation: Shura and civic participation both encourage consultation and responsible decision-making for the common good.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze Islamic governance principles in relation to civic participation.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion best explains why isnad and matn are both examined in Hadith studies?
options: A report needs reliable transmission and meaningful content for proper evaluation
Only the number of words matters
All reports are accepted without checking
The chain of narrators replaces the text completely
questions.correctAnswer: A report needs reliable transmission and meaningful content for proper evaluation
questions.explanation: Hadith evaluation considers both who transmitted the report and what the report says.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze why both transmission and content matter in Hadith studies.

questions.prompt: A Muslim students' club wants to conduct Da'wah during an interfaith week. Which plan is most ethical?
options: Prepare factual displays, invite questions, and respect every visitor's dignity
Interrupt other groups' presentations
Use fear and insults to force agreement
Hide the purpose of the event from the school
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare factual displays, invite questions, and respect every visitor's dignity
questions.explanation: Ethical Da'wah should be truthful, respectful, peaceful, and suitable for a multi-faith environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Select an ethical plan for explaining Islamic teachings in a multi-faith setting.

questions.prompt: Which policy would best apply Islamic labour ethics in a school-based business project?
options: Written duties, safe conditions, fair pay, and honest records
Unpaid work with no consent
Hidden deductions from workers' pay
Favouritism instead of agreed criteria
questions.correctAnswer: Written duties, safe conditions, fair pay, and honest records
questions.explanation: A practical labour policy should reflect fairness, safety, transparency, and fulfilment of agreements.
questions.learningOutcome: Design ethical labour practices using Islamic principles.

questions.prompt: Which factor contributed to the decline of the Umayyad dynasty?
options: Political opposition and internal tensions over governance
The invention of printing in Europe
The Exodus from Egypt
The writing of the Bhagavad Gita
questions.correctAnswer: Political opposition and internal tensions over governance
questions.explanation: The Umayyad decline involved political, social, and administrative challenges that weakened the dynasty.
questions.subStrandTitle: Achievements and Decline of the Umayyad Dynasty
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze factors that contributed to the decline of the Umayyad dynasty.

questions.prompt: A learner must choose a source for explaining the context of a Qur'anic verse. Which source is most suitable?
options: A reliable tafsir or teacher explaining Asbab al-Nuzul
A social media joke about the verse
A random translation with no background
A chart about Old Testament prophets
questions.correctAnswer: A reliable tafsir or teacher explaining Asbab al-Nuzul
questions.explanation: Reliable context helps prevent careless interpretation and supports accurate learning.
questions.strandTitle: IRE: Study of the Qur'an and Hadith
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate reliable sources for understanding reasons for revelation.

questions.prompt: Which combined class project best synthesizes Grade 10 IRE values of honesty, consultation, and social welfare?
options: A transparent charity drive planned through consultation and audited by learners
A secret collection with no records
A debate where only one learner is allowed to speak
A competition to shame families needing support
questions.correctAnswer: A transparent charity drive planned through consultation and audited by learners
questions.explanation: The project combines Akhlaq, shura, accountability, and care for vulnerable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a project that integrates Islamic values in community service.

questions.prompt: In Grade 10 HRE, what does Paramatma generally refer to?
options: The Supreme Self or ultimate divine reality
A musical drum used only in folk dance
A type of classroom timetable
A market tax on goods
questions.correctAnswer: The Supreme Self or ultimate divine reality
questions.explanation: HRE studies Paramatma as a central concept in understanding divine reality in Hindu traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Define Paramatma in the context of Hindu Religious Education.

questions.prompt: Which three deities are commonly associated with the Trimurti?
options: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva
Moses, Elijah, and Amos
Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman
Matthew, Mark, and Luke
questions.correctAnswer: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva
questions.explanation: The Trimurti is commonly understood through Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver, and Shiva the transformer.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the deities commonly linked with the Trimurti.

questions.prompt: A learner treats Dashavatar stories as entertainment only. Which response best analyses their Grade 10 HRE purpose?
options: To learn how divine manifestations teach protection of dharma and moral order
To memorize a list of modern political parties
To replace all study of scriptures
To classify musical instruments only
questions.correctAnswer: To learn how divine manifestations teach protection of dharma and moral order
questions.explanation: Dashavatar stories are studied for their religious meaning and ethical lessons about restoring balance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze moral lessons associated with Dashavatar narratives.

questions.prompt: In Jain tradition, what is a Tirthankar?
options: An enlightened teacher who shows a path of liberation
A king who standardizes Qur'anic recitation
A prophet from the Old Testament
A Christian sacrament
questions.correctAnswer: An enlightened teacher who shows a path of liberation
questions.explanation: Tirthankars are revered teachers in Jain tradition who guide followers toward liberation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the meaning and role of a Tirthankar in Jain tradition.

questions.prompt: Which value is strongly emphasized in Jain teachings connected with Tirthankars?
options: Ahimsa, or non-violence
Revenge against rivals
Wasteful use of resources
Forced conversion
questions.correctAnswer: Ahimsa, or non-violence
questions.explanation: Jain ethical teaching strongly emphasizes non-violence, self-control, truthfulness, and respect for life.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain values taught through Jain Tirthankars.

questions.prompt: Which idea is central to Buddhist views studied in HRE?
options: Reducing suffering through wisdom, ethical conduct, and mental discipline
Seeking wealth as the only goal of life
Rejecting compassion as weakness
Measuring worship by noise alone
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing suffering through wisdom, ethical conduct, and mental discipline
questions.explanation: Buddhist teachings commonly emphasize understanding suffering, ethical conduct, compassion, and discipline.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe key ethical ideas in Buddhist views studied in HRE.

questions.prompt: In the Sikh faith, what does Guru's Grace help learners understand?
options: The role of the Guru in guiding spiritual growth and service
The rules for the Sinai Covenant
The classification of Umayyad caliphs
The location of Galilean towns only
questions.correctAnswer: The role of the Guru in guiding spiritual growth and service
questions.explanation: Sikh teaching values the Guru's guidance, remembrance of God, honest living, and service.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of Guru's Grace in Sikh tradition.

questions.prompt: Which scripture is central in Sikh tradition?
options: Guru Granth Sahib
Book of Amos
First Corinthians
Sahih al-Bukhari
questions.correctAnswer: Guru Granth Sahib
questions.explanation: The Guru Granth Sahib is the central scripture and spiritual guide in Sikh tradition.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major scriptures studied in Hindu Religious Education.

questions.prompt: Which set includes scriptures commonly studied in HRE across Hindu traditions?
options: Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and epics
Gospels, Acts, Epistles, and Revelation
Isnad, Matn, Zakat, and Shura
Maps, ledgers, contracts, and minutes
questions.correctAnswer: Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and epics
questions.explanation: HRE examines sacred texts and their ethical teachings across Sanatan, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Name examples of scriptures studied in HRE.

questions.prompt: What is the main value of studying ethical and moral teachings in HRE scriptures?
options: They guide personal conduct, service, and respect for life
They remove the need for personal responsibility
They encourage discrimination against other faiths
They are studied only for spelling practice
questions.correctAnswer: They guide personal conduct, service, and respect for life
questions.explanation: Scriptural teachings support moral growth, self-discipline, compassion, and social responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how scriptural teachings guide ethical living.

questions.prompt: Which prominent personality is associated with the founding of Sikhism?
options: Guru Nanak
Prophet Amos
Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan
Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Guru Nanak
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak is revered as the founder and first Guru of Sikhism.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify prominent personalities connected with traditions studied in HRE.

questions.prompt: What does dharma generally mean in HRE?
options: Righteous duty, moral order, and responsible way of living
A tax collected in a market
A type of written examination
A rule against all music
questions.correctAnswer: Righteous duty, moral order, and responsible way of living
questions.explanation: Dharma refers to duty and moral order that guide right conduct in life.
questions.learningOutcome: Define dharma as a core concept in HRE.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation of the Law of Karma is most complete for moral decision-making?
options: Actions have consequences that shape moral and spiritual progress
Luck alone controls every outcome
No action has moral value
Only public actions matter while private actions do not
questions.correctAnswer: Actions have consequences that shape moral and spiritual progress
questions.explanation: Karma teaches responsibility for actions, intentions, and their effects.
questions.subStrandTitle: Introduction to the Law of Karma
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the Law of Karma and its moral implications.

questions.prompt: A learner refuses to spread a harmful rumour because they believe actions have consequences. Which HRE concept is being applied?
options: Karma
Kafan
Pentecost
Isnad
questions.correctAnswer: Karma
questions.explanation: The learner is applying the idea that choices and intentions carry moral consequences.
questions.subStrandTitle: Introduction to the Law of Karma
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the Law of Karma to everyday moral choices.

questions.prompt: Which practice best reflects dharma in a school environment?
options: Doing assigned duties honestly while respecting others
Ignoring responsibilities when teachers are absent
Damaging shared property for fun
Mocking learners from other communities
questions.correctAnswer: Doing assigned duties honestly while respecting others
questions.explanation: Dharma includes fulfilling duties responsibly and acting in ways that support moral order.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply dharma to responsible conduct in school life.

questions.prompt: What is vocal music in the HRE cultural practices strand?
options: Music produced mainly through singing
Music produced only by drums
Silent written prayer
A record of legal cases
questions.correctAnswer: Music produced mainly through singing
questions.explanation: Vocal music focuses on the voice and may include devotional and classical forms.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify vocal music as a cultural practice in HRE.

questions.prompt: Which item is an example of an instrument used in Indian musical traditions?
options: Tabla
Microscope
Compass
Bunsen burner
questions.correctAnswer: Tabla
questions.explanation: The tabla is a percussion instrument associated with Indian music traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of instruments used in Indian music traditions.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best analyses why HRE studies both folk and classical dances?
options: They express cultural identity, devotion, values, and community memory
They replace all ethical teaching
They are used only for sports scoring
They have no connection to culture
questions.correctAnswer: They express cultural identity, devotion, values, and community memory
questions.explanation: Dance can communicate stories, devotion, discipline, and cultural heritage.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the cultural and religious value of dance traditions.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows respect when observing a worship practice from another tradition during HRE learning?
options: Listen carefully, ask polite questions, and avoid ridicule
Laugh at unfamiliar words
Interrupt to prove superiority
Record people secretly without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Listen carefully, ask polite questions, and avoid ridicule
questions.explanation: Religious education should build respect, careful observation, and peaceful coexistence.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful conduct when learning about religious traditions.

questions.prompt: Which comparison best distinguishes folk dance from classical dance in HRE cultural practices?
options: Folk dance is community-based while classical dance usually follows formal training and codified styles
Folk dance is always written in a laboratory while classical dance is never performed
Folk dance belongs only to one family while classical dance has no rules
Folk dance is a scripture and classical dance is a tax
questions.correctAnswer: Folk dance is community-based while classical dance usually follows formal training and codified styles
questions.explanation: Folk dances often arise from community life, while classical dances tend to use formal techniques and traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare folk and classical dance forms as cultural practices.

questions.prompt: How can the Law of Karma encourage environmental responsibility?
options: It reminds learners that harmful actions toward nature have consequences
It teaches that pollution has no moral meaning
It supports wasting resources for status
It discourages care for living beings
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds learners that harmful actions toward nature have consequences
questions.explanation: Karma can be applied to choices that affect people, living beings, and the environment.
questions.subStrandTitle: Introduction to the Law of Karma
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the Law of Karma to environmental responsibility.

questions.prompt: A group studies Sanatan, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh teachings together. What HRE skill are they mainly developing?
options: Comparative understanding with respect for diversity
Refusal to learn from unfamiliar traditions
Memorization of one tradition while mocking others
Avoidance of all moral questions
questions.correctAnswer: Comparative understanding with respect for diversity
questions.explanation: HRE helps learners compare traditions respectfully and recognize shared values and differences.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare ethical teachings across traditions studied in HRE.

questions.prompt: Which statement best links ahimsa and respectful speech?
options: Non-violence includes avoiding words that harm others
Non-violence concerns only physical injuries
Respectful speech is unrelated to moral conduct
Harsh speech is required in every debate
questions.correctAnswer: Non-violence includes avoiding words that harm others
questions.explanation: Ahimsa can guide both actions and speech by reducing harm and encouraging compassion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ahimsa to speech and relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner studies the same value of compassion in Buddhist teachings and Sikh service. Which thinking skill is being used?
options: Comparing ethical teachings across traditions
Ignoring all similarities
Copying without understanding
Changing the subject to mathematics
questions.correctAnswer: Comparing ethical teachings across traditions
questions.explanation: Comparative study helps learners recognize shared values while respecting each tradition's context.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze shared ethical values across HRE traditions.

questions.prompt: Which plan best applies dharma during a class leadership election?
options: Campaign honestly, respect opponents, and accept fair results
Spread lies to gain votes
Bribe classmates with gifts
Threaten learners who ask questions
questions.correctAnswer: Campaign honestly, respect opponents, and accept fair results
questions.explanation: Dharma supports truthfulness, duty, self-control, and respect in public responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate how dharma guides ethical leadership choices.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion best explains why scriptures are studied together with prominent personalities in HRE?
options: Personalities show how teachings can be lived in real communities
Personalities replace all scriptures
Scriptures have no ethical content
Historical people are studied only for dates
questions.correctAnswer: Personalities show how teachings can be lived in real communities
questions.explanation: Prominent personalities help learners connect sacred teachings with lived examples and moral choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how prominent personalities demonstrate scriptural values.

questions.prompt: A learner says karma means people should ignore those suffering because they deserve it. Which response best corrects this misunderstanding?
options: Karma teaches responsibility, but compassion and service remain moral duties
Karma means help is always forbidden
Karma removes all concern for justice
Karma applies only to exam results
questions.correctAnswer: Karma teaches responsibility, but compassion and service remain moral duties
questions.explanation: HRE should avoid blaming victims; moral responsibility is joined with compassion, service, and justice.
questions.subStrandTitle: Introduction to the Law of Karma
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate misunderstandings of karma using ethical reasoning.

questions.prompt: Which school cultural event plan best respects HRE learning on music and dance?
options: Invite informed presenters, explain meanings, credit traditions, and keep performances respectful
Turn sacred songs into jokes
Use costumes without learning their meaning
Exclude learners who ask cultural questions
questions.correctAnswer: Invite informed presenters, explain meanings, credit traditions, and keep performances respectful
questions.explanation: Cultural practices should be handled with accuracy, respect, permission, and appreciation for meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Design respectful ways to present cultural practices in a school setting.

questions.prompt: Which project best brings together HRE concepts of ahimsa, dharma, and karma?
options: A peer-support programme that promotes non-violence, duty, and responsible choices
A prank competition that rewards humiliation
A clean-up campaign with no safety rules
A debate that bans listening to others
questions.correctAnswer: A peer-support programme that promotes non-violence, duty, and responsible choices
questions.explanation: The project integrates non-harm, responsible duty, and awareness of consequences.
questions.subStrandTitle: Core Beliefs and Law of Karma
questions.learningOutcome: Select a project that integrates key HRE ethical concepts.

questions.prompt: Which inquiry question would best guide Grade 10 learners studying Trimurti and Dashavatars?
options: How do different manifestations teach moral responsibility and restoration of order?
How can learners avoid studying religious stories?
Which story can be used to mock another faith?
How many marks can be gained without understanding?
questions.correctAnswer: How do different manifestations teach moral responsibility and restoration of order?
questions.explanation: A strong inquiry question invites analysis of meaning, values, and application.
questions.learningOutcome: Formulate inquiry around moral lessons in manifestations of Paramatma.

questions.prompt: Which option best evaluates the role of vocal and instrumental music in HRE cultural practices?
options: They can support devotion, memory, discipline, and community identity
They are studied only because they are loud
They have no cultural or spiritual meaning
They replace all scripture and ethics
questions.correctAnswer: They can support devotion, memory, discipline, and community identity
questions.explanation: Music can carry values, devotion, discipline, and cultural heritage in religious communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate the religious and cultural functions of music.

questions.prompt: Which response best applies Buddhist emphasis on compassion to a school conflict?
options: Listen to both sides, reduce harm, and seek a peaceful solution
Encourage revenge so the conflict grows
Ignore the pain of those affected
Laugh at the weaker learner
questions.correctAnswer: Listen to both sides, reduce harm, and seek a peaceful solution
questions.explanation: Compassion in conflict seeks understanding, reduced harm, and peaceful resolution.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Buddhist ethical ideas to peaceful conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: A Grade 10 HRE class wants to document local Hindu, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh cultural practices. Which method is most ethical?
options: Seek consent, ask respectful questions, verify meanings, and protect privacy
Record ceremonies secretly and post them online
Invent explanations without asking practitioners
Interview only one person and claim to represent everyone
questions.correctAnswer: Seek consent, ask respectful questions, verify meanings, and protect privacy
questions.explanation: Ethical inquiry requires respect, consent, accuracy, and care for participants' dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an ethical inquiry into religious and cultural practices.
